text:
jen: Heads-up: after yesterday's deploy we saw queue lengths spike on p3dn nodes for small chat-ish requests. Root cause looks like batching heuristic shifted token_budget target up. Posting quick perf traces.

miguel: Can you paste the traces? did KV cache miss rate change?

jen: trace: https://perf.internal/trace/rt-2026-03-16-abc123 

jen: Key observations: avg batch size increased from ~4 -> ~9 for requests with seq<=32; p95 latency for single-turn flows bumped ~40%. KV cache hit rate dropped ~12% for short prompts.

sam: That matches alerts: runtime-worker queue wait >120ms across the fleet. Edge started returning more 429s due to soft-limit gating.

tara: Was the queue admission policy changed in the rollout? I saw a diff referencing `prefer_fill=true`.

jen: yes — we switched prefer_fill=true to improve throughput for long runs; it uses token_budget target 768 by default. For short requests that's overshooting and forces larger batches.

noah: Suggest we lower token_budget for latency-sensitive routes. Maybe dynamic_budget = min(ceil(expected_tokens * 1.2), max_budget).

miguel: Also, when batches grow, KV cache locality suffers: batched requests more likely to touch different KV prefixes so hit rates drop. We should bias batch formation to favor same-KV-session when possible.

jen: Proposed hotfix config (canary):
```yaml
queue_admission:
  mode: soft
  soft_limit: 0.7
  reject_threshold: 0.95
  token_budget_override:
    short: 256
    default: 512
  prefer_fill: false
```

sam: Can we gate this behind a rollout flag and enable for demo/low-risk routes first?

tara: yes. I'll coordinate a canary in eu-west-1. Plan: canary 10% -> 25% -> 100% if metrics look good.

miguel: What metrics are we watching? Propose: p95 latency (short routes), KV hit rate, median batch size, 429/sec, and cpu utilization.

noah: Add gen_quality metric too: gen_token_loss on our evals so we catch any sampling/quality regressions after admission changes.

jen: After deploying the patch to 10% canary: batch size for short routes dropped to ~3, p95 latency recovered ~30ms, KV hit returned to baseline.

sam: We did see a slight CPU inefficiency — more small kernel invocations — but cost per request improved because fewer extra tokens were generated and fewer retries/clients timed out.

tara: Recommendation: also push a backpressure signal to the edge so non-critical clients get a 429 earlier instead of piling up in runtime queues.

jen: Edge change we tested: return 429 with Retry-After=0.25 when queue depth > soft_limit * capacity. That shaves off long tails.

miguel: Consider a 'soft-shed' mode: accept request but return an abbreviated result or fast-fail with partial generation. Might be useful for telemetry endpoints but risky for product correctness.

noah: Partial gen is risky for downstream apps. For now prefer clear 429s and let clients retry/backoff.

sam: Plan summary: 1) canary queue_admission patch today 15:30 UTC in eu-west-1 (10%), 2) watch the listed metrics for 2h, 3) expand to 25% if stable, 4) push minimal edge 429 gating. @tara to coordinate rollout.

tara: On it — dashboard updated and alert thresholds adjusted. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: Canary rollout started for runtime-service:v2.3.4 to eu-west-1 (10%)

jen: Thanks all. I'll follow up with a doc outlining long-term changes: token-aware batching, KV-session affinity in batch formation, queue admission policy tuning (soft vs hard limits), and richer backpressure metrics.

sam: sgtm

noah: TY

miguel: good catch — glad we caught this in canary
